deep.reconstruction:
This is a working sheet for Riemann's 1859 memoir 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse'. In Riemann's notation Π(s-1)=Γ(s), so Π(x)=Γ(x+1).

(A) Integral representation. ζ(s)=Σ n^{-s}. Substituting x→nx in Γ(s)=∫_0^∞ e^{-x}x^{s-1}dx gives ∫_0^∞ e^{-nx}x^{s-1}dx = Γ(s) n^{-s}. Summing the geometric series: Γ(s)ζ(s)=∫_0^∞ e^{-x}/(1-e^{-x}) x^{s-1}dx = ∫_0^∞ x^{s-1}/(e^x-1)dx, valid for Re s>1. The page writes 'Πs' for the Gamma factor; the side note 1/(s-1) and ∫e^{-x}x^{s-1}dx are scratch work. Also noted is the general partial-fraction rule 1/φ(x)=Σ 1/(φ'(α)(x-α)) over the roots α of φ.

(B) Loop integral. Integrate x^{s-1}/(e^x-1) along a path that comes from +∞, circles 0 and returns to +∞ (drawn on the page as a loop around 0 inside a large circle). Take arg x from 0 to 2π. The two sides of the cut give (e^{2πis}-1)Γ(s)ζ(s) = e^{πis}·2i sin(πs)·Γ(s)ζ(s). This matches the page's 'Πs ζ(s) e^{πsi} 2 sin sπ i = ∫_∞^∞ x^{s-1}dx/(e^x-1)', up to orientation.

(C) Functional equation by residues. The poles of 1/(e^x-1) are x=2nπi. Riemann expands 1/(e^x-1)=1/x+Σ_{n≠0} 1/(x-2nπi). (My note: the constant -1/2 is omitted; it does not affect the outcome for Re s<0.) For Re s<0 the loop is opened to the large circle. Each pole contributes, up to sign, 2πi·(2nπi)^{s-1} = 2πi·n^{s-1}2^{s-1}π^{s-1}i^{s-1}, with i^{s-1}=e^{iπ(s-1)/2}. The conjugate poles carry (-i)^{s-1}, which the page writes as e^{-iπ(s-1)/2}; on the branch arg∈(0,2π) it is e^{3iπ(s-1)/2}.

Adding the two families (my completion): (2π)^{s-1}·2πi·ζ(1-s)·e^{iπ(s-1)}·2cos(π(s-1)/2). Cancelling the common unit factors gives
 sin(πs) Γ(s) ζ(s) = (2π)^s cos(π(s-1)/2) ζ(1-s).
This is the page's line 'ζ(1-s) cos(π/2)(s-1) (2π)^s'. Since cos(π(s-1)/2)=sin(πs/2) and sin πs = 2 sin(πs/2)cos(πs/2), it is equivalent to ζ(1-s)=2(2π)^{-s}cos(πs/2)Γ(s)ζ(s), the functional equation. Π(1-x²/p²) appears as a side product, presumably a sine-type product.

(D) Euler product and logarithmic derivative.
- log ζ(s) = -Σ_p log(1-p^{-s}).
- ζ'/ζ(s) = Σ_p p^{-s}(-log p)/(1-p^{-s}).
- With f the prime-counting step function (or its density), this is written as an integral -∫_a^∞ f(x) log x dx/(x^s-1), roughly of the form ∫ (1/(x^s-1)) f(x) log x.
- The comparison integral ∫_1^∞ dx/(x^s-1) = Σ_k ∫_1^∞ x^{-ks}dx = Σ_k 1/(ks-1), listed as 1/(s-1), 1/(2s-1), 1/(3s-1), ...
- Subtracting it gives ζ'/ζ - ∫dx/(x^s-1) = ∫ (f(x)log x - 1)/(x^s-1) dx. This compares primes with the density 1/log x.
- Side sums Σp^{-s}, Σp^{-2s}, Σp^{-3s}, Σ1/p², Σ1/p⁴ are the prime-power layers.

(E) Möbius inversion. Riemann sets ψ(s)=ζ(s)+ζ(2s)+ζ(3s)+…. He notes ψ(s)-ψ(2s) leaves ζ(s)+ζ(3s)+ζ(5s)+…, then continues the sieve: -ψ(3s)+ψ(6s)-ψ(5s)+ψ(10s)+ψ(15s)-ψ(30s)…. That is, ζ(s)=Σ_k μ(k)ψ(ks).

The same sieve is applied to the densities ψ(n):=x^{1/n-1}/log x. These satisfy d/dx Li(x^{1/n}) = x^{1/n-1}/log x. The Möbius pattern ψ(1)-ψ(2)-ψ(3)-ψ(5)+ψ(6)-ψ(7)… is written out, with the weight 1/n noted separately. In integrated form: ∫_a^b dx/log x, ∫_{a^{1/2}}^{b^{1/2}} dx/log x, ∫_{a^{1/3}}^{b^{1/3}} dx/log x, i.e. Li(x^{1/n}) terms. The entries x-x^{1/2}, x+x^{1/2} and 1/log x - x^{-1/2}/log x are trial first corrections.

This is the germ of the memoir's π(x)=Σ μ(n)/n f(x^{1/n}) and of Li(x)-½Li(x^{1/2})-…. The previous page's '0 = 1-1/2-1/3+1/5+1/6-1/7…' is Σμ(n)/n=0 (the correct sign of 1/5 is minus). Π(1-1/p) appears again.

(F) Digamma. d log Π(x)/dx = ψ(x) and ψ(x)=1/x+ψ(x-1), Gauss's digamma in Π-notation.

(G) Partial zeta. ψ(n,s)=Σ_{k=1}^n k^{-s}, with Γ(s)ψ(n,s)=Σ_{k=1}^n ∫e^{-kx}x^{s-1}dx = ∫_0^∞ (e^{-x}-e^{-(n+1)x})/(1-e^{-x}) x^{s-1}dx (finite geometric sum).

(H) Zeros of Euler factors. 1-p^{-s}=0 ⇔ s log p = 2πin, so log p/n = 2πi/s =: log x and x=p^{1/n}. This locates the purely imaginary poles of each term of ζ'/ζ on Re s=0, i.e. 1-p^{-s} on the imaginary axis.

'∫dQ/(a+t)' is an isolated, unclear note.
errors: The Gamma factor is written 'Π s' (also 'Πs ψ(n,s)'); in Riemann's own notation it should be Π(s-1)=Γ(s). This is a notational slip.
The partial fraction 1/(e^x-1)=1/x+Σ1/(x-2nπi) omits the constant -1/2 and the symmetric pairing needed for convergence. This is harmless for the loop integral when Re s<0.

The conjugate branch factor is written e^{-iπ(s-1)/2}. On the cut arg∈(0,2π) it is e^{3iπ(s-1)/2}; the unit factors e^{iπ(s-1)}, i and the signs are not fully tracked. The final relation sin(πs)Γ(s)ζ(s)=(2π)^s cos(π(s-1)/2)ζ(1-s) is nevertheless correct.
'ψ(s)-ψ(2s)=ζ(s)' is false as written: it equals ζ(s)+ζ(3s)+ζ(5s)+…. Riemann evidently treats it as the first step of a sieve, continued by -ψ(3s)+ψ(6s)-ψ(5s)+….
ψ(s)=Σ_k ζ(ks) diverges, since ζ(ks)→1. The inversion is formal, or should be applied to ζ(ks)-1 or to the prime-power sums; the same inversion is valid for the prime-power density sums.
'1/log x - x^{1/2-1}/log x' lacks the factor 1/2: the density of ½Li(x^{1/2}) is x^{-1/2}/(2 log x). The 1/n weights are noted separately ('1/n').
Lower and upper limits are both 'a' in ∫_a^a dx/log x; it is presumably ∫_a^b.
Previous page: the sign of 1/5 in 1-1/2-1/3+1/5+1/6-1/7 should be minus (μ(5)=-1).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the derivations published in Riemann's 1859 memoir: the integral representation, the contour proof of the functional equation, the Euler product with logarithmic derivative, and the Möbius inversion leading to the Li(x^{1/n}) terms. It is well known as his, and these Nachlass sheets were studied by Siegel and others. Its value is only in showing the working process (sign slips, the -1/2 dropped from the partial fractions, the formal ψ-sieve).

transcription_corrections: 'Πs ζ(s)' / 'Πs ψ(n,s)': the Gamma factor, properly Π(s-1)=Γ(s) in Riemann's notation.
'2 sin sπ i' means 2i·sin(πs), not sin(sπi).
'1/e^x = Σ 1/(φ'(α)(x-α))' is the general partial-fraction formula 1/φ(x)=Σ1/(φ'(α)(x-α)), applied to φ=e^x-1.
'∫_a^a dx/log x' should be ∫_a^b dx/log x.
'1 - e^{s log p}' is most likely 1 - p^{-s} = 1 - e^{-s log p}.
'log p s = n2πi' means s·log p = 2nπi.
'ψ(s) = Σ_1^n 1/n^s' is the partial sum ψ(n,s)=Σ_{k=1}^n k^{-s}.
The stray 'π' after the first integral is probably not part of a formula.
The bottom line of the contour sum reads ζ(1-s) cos(π/2)(s-1) (2π)^s, with the factor (2π)^s possibly written (2π)^{s-1}·2π.
